practice.title: What I Do In Practice
practice.subtitle: From architecture to interaction logic to production code.

intro: Torchyan started from a simple observation: digital projects lose quality at the handoffs — between strategy and design, design and code, launch and everything after.
So I run each project as one continuous chain, and stay responsible for all of it.
I use AI tools every day to research, prototype and build faster. The judgement, the design decisions and the accountability stay human.
The goal: websites and products that work the way they were designed to — and keep improving after launch.

hero.title: Picsart
hero.subtitle: Growth & Marketplace — UI engineering at product scale
description: From October 2021 to February 2024, I worked as a Senior UI Engineer on picsart.com — first with the Growth team, then with Marketplace.
The work: integrating the Picsart Design System, building the components it didn’t cover, adding right-to-left language support from scratch, and a large part of the accessibility work in my scope.

timeline.title: What the work involved
subtitle: picsart.com is a large product surface, shipped by many teams at once.
My job was to keep the UI in my team’s scope consistent, accessible and ready for every language.

steps.title: Context
blocks: Picsart’s website serves many products and page types:
Marketing and business pages
Marketplace and Discovery
The editor and Mini Apps
Growth products such as Ad Wizard
Many teams ship to picsart.com at once. Each team has one person responsible for Design System integration — in my team’s scope, that was me.

steps.title: Growth team, 2021–2023
blocks: I was the team’s primary UI developer, focused on the Picsart website:
Modular, scalable UI in React, JSS and Styled Components
Responsive, cross-browser implementation
Accessibility work
Code reviews for performance, maintainability and best practice

steps.title: Ad Wizard
blocks: A separate Growth product where people create visual and social content and adapt it to the formats each platform needs — text, imagery, titles and emoji in one editor.
As the Growth team’s primary UI developer, I implemented its interface in React, HTML/CSS, JSS and Styled Components.

steps.title: Design System integration
blocks: I was the main UI and Design System integration owner for picsart.com and selected product branches in my team:
Integrated shared components across business pages, the editor and Mini Apps
Placed supplied components and templates as product required

steps.title: Components the system didn’t cover
blocks: The shared components came from the Design System team.
When a need wasn’t covered, I built the missing components for our product branch, matched to the system so the product still felt like one.

steps.title: Right-to-left languages
blocks: I implemented multilingual support, including RTL/LTR, from scratch for my scope.
Instead of fixing left and right values page by page, I reworked layout direction around logical properties — inline and block, start and end — so a change of direction carries through the structure.

steps.title: Accessibility
blocks: Accessibility was only minimally in place when I started. I handled a large part of the WCAG implementation work in my scope, building it into components rather than adding it afterwards.

steps.title: Responsive and cross-browser
blocks: Every component checked across breakpoints and browsers, so pages behaved the same for every visitor.

steps.title: Performance
blocks: On the Growth team, I optimized the Discovery pages and their codebase.
Pages were measured before and after; the figures aren’t published here.

steps.title: What changed
blocks: Right-to-left languages supported structurally, not by manual fixes
Marketplace pages consistent with the shared Design System
Accessibility built into components in my scope
Faster Discovery pages

steps.title: What this shows
blocks: Work at product scale, inside large teams and shared systems
Localization and accessibility treated as structure, not patches
The same standards applied to every Torchyan project

blueprint.title: Integration principles
blueprint.subtitle: How the shared Design System was carried into the pages in my scope.

cards.title: Shared first
cards.body: Use Design System components wherever they fit; build new ones only for real gaps.

cards.title: Match the system
cards.body: New components follow the shared tokens, spacing and states.

cards.title: Direction-agnostic layout
cards.body: Logical properties instead of left and right, so RTL works structurally.

cards.title: Accessible by default
cards.body: Accessibility considered in every component, not added later.

cards.title: Responsive everywhere
cards.body: Every component checked across breakpoints and browsers.

architecture.title: In detail
architecture.subtitle: Five parts of the work, and how each was approached.

useCases.title: 1. RTL/LTR layout logic
blocks: Switching a page between left-to-right and right-to-left usually means hunting down every left and right value.
I rebuilt the layout direction around logical properties:
margin-inline and padding-inline instead of left and right
inset-inline-start and inset-inline-end for positioning
Direction set once, at the root
A direction change now carries through the structure instead of being patched page by page.

useCases.title: 2. Design System integration
blocks: Shared components from the Design System team, integrated across:
Business and product pages
The editor
Mini Apps
Placement followed product direction; consistency across branches was my responsibility in my team’s scope.

useCases.title: 3. Components the system didn’t cover
blocks: Some Marketplace needs weren’t in the shared system. For those, I built team-specific components that:
Use the shared tokens
Follow the same states and spacing
Stay responsive and accessible

useCases.title: 4. Accessibility implementation
blocks: From a minimal starting point, accessibility became part of the components in my scope rather than a late fix. I handled a large part of that WCAG implementation work myself.

useCases.title: 5. Ad Wizard
blocks: A separate Growth product for creating visual and social content and adapting it to each platform’s formats. As the team’s primary UI developer, I implemented its interface in React, HTML/CSS, JSS and Styled Components.
